newsitem.title: UK: Carlton, CableTel plan bid for digital TV -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Carlton, CableTel plan bid for digital TV -- paper.

text.p: Carlton Communications Plc and cable television operator International CableTel Inc plan to bid for licences to operate new digital terrestrial television channels in Britain, a London newspaper reported on Tuesday.

British media concern Carlton and CableTel, a U.S.-based cable television operator which also operates in the UK, are in talks with programmers, including Flextech Plc, to reach preliminary agreements prior to January 31, 1997, the deadline for applications for the licences, the Independent reported.
Flextech, a programmer for cable and satellite television, is majority owned by Tele-Communications Inc, the largest U.S. cable operator.

The Independent, which gave no source for its report, said the programming talks, which remain at an early stage, could include making Flextech's joint venture channels with the BBC exclusive to Carlton or to CableTel.
Flextech is believed to have reserved the right to offer the channels for broadcast on other digital platforms, the newspaper said.
